This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bebbb726f13566c509d5cb45b4754137b6992d6d` — the merge of head `a50b8dce07a691b25c02837e77af204d0cc7105b` into base `14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bebbb726f13566c509d5cb45b4754137b6992d6d && git checkout bebbb726f13566c509d5cb45b4754137b6992d6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562 a50b8dce07a691b25c02837e77af204d0cc7105b && git checkout -B drift-repro 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562 && git merge --no-ff a50b8dce07a691b25c02837e77af204d0cc7105b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 14208f2c504ff6f1529be8a28323a91df53d0562` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a50b8dce07a691b25c02837e77af204d0cc7105b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.text-shape.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/operator-object-write-value.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`), packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES`, `isMultiValueField`), packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts (`invalid_value_shape`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the insert / update / multi-update validator calls), packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/auth-event-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/action-invocation-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/key-material-copy-migration.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/suspended-run-store.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/sql-http-outbox.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/field-file-service.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/migration-flag.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-metadata-decode.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/SignatureField.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/QRCodeField.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/RichTextField.tsx, .changeset/29133-text-field-refuses-object-array.md (prose face, read for the ② declaration lines)

Narrowing face (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at line start of the PR body and of the changeset): `reviewFace` returns no `hits` for these paths, so the Scope floor is every non-prose path of the diff, listed first above. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; implementation claim names the branch.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Create door narrows — correct.** On main the `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` arm (record-validator.ts, the string branch) judged `s = String(value)` against bounds / domain / format and never asked whether `value` was a string, so `{ nested: true }` and `['a','b']` on any of the twelve types passed (`"[object Object]"` is 15 chars, `"a,b"` is 3) and reached the driver as sent. On head the arm returns `fail('invalid_type', { type, detail: 'expected a string, received an object|an array' }, 'invalid_value_shape')` before any bound. Reached by `engine.insert` (engine.ts: `validateRecordInScope(…, 'insert', 'include')`), the REST POST that calls it, a flow `create_record`, and the dry run / `os validate` seed walk (engine-validate.ts:548, cli `seed-record-values`). Pinned for all 12 × {object, array, {}, []} × {insert, update} in the new suite.
2. **Update and multi-update doors narrow — correct.** `engine.update` first pass calls `validateRecord(updateSchema, data, 'update')` (engine.ts:17846 / 18264) for the single and `multi: true` branches alike; the new end-to-end case drives both through a recording driver and asserts the driver sees no write. The screen-flow resume (card step 3) lands through the same `engine.update`; the dev pinned the engine door rather than the HTTP route, which is the right seam since nothing between the route and the validator reads the value.
3. **Readonly scope narrows too — correct and consistent.** The check is placed before `if (shapeOnly) return null`, so a readonly text-family field's value under the `'include'` (insert final payload, dry run) and `'only'` (update second pass, post-strip) scopes is now refused for a plain object or array where it was admitted. This is one accept-set change the card did not name; it is right by the `ReadonlyValueScope` contract ("the per-type arms that ask 'is this a value of the declared type at all'"), and the number, boolean, date and multi-value arms already refuse their wrong shape in `shapeOnly`. The docblock at record-validator.ts:672 is updated to list it.
4. **Nothing else changes — verified.** A string, a number and a boolean still take their `String(value)` reading (pinned); `null` / `undefined` return at `isMissing` before the arm; `json` and the structured-JSON class never enter the arm; a filter-operator object is still refused one branch earlier with its own sentence (`valueMayBeAnObject` is false for every string type, so the `$in` rule runs first; pinned). No string type is in `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` (`select, radio, lookup, user, file, image`) or `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES`, so there is no `multiple: true` text field whose array this refusal could take away. A `Date` or other class instance is not a plain object (`isPlainObjectValue` requires `Object.prototype` or a null prototype) and keeps its coercion — unchanged, noted for completeness.
5. **Wire surface unchanged — verified.** Code `invalid_type` and message key `invalid_value_shape` (`{{label}} has an invalid {{type}} value: {{detail}}`) both exist on main in all four bundles (validation-message.ts:153/202/248/294); only the `detail` text is new. No `packages/spec` edit, no export change.
6. **Forced test edit — intent kept.** The two `#5922` "leaves alone" pins asserted that the operator rule is derived from the operator vocabulary, not the `$` sigil, by writing `{ $inn: … }` / `{ a: 1 }` into `title` (text) and expecting admission. On head that admission no longer exists for text, so leaving them would make them fail for a reason unrelated to the operator rule. Moving them to `stage_free` (a `select` with no `options`, already in that schema, and the one scalar type the #5922 table records as still ADMITTING a plain object) keeps the assertion about the operator rule intact. The comment explains the move and cites the new suite.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is declared at line start in the PR body and the changeset, with the measurement. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no schema key, accepted metadata value, export or type moves; only a record write of the wrong shape is refused. Per AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist level table a non-protocol narrowing ships **`patch`** and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition: the changeset is `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, carries the `**BREAKING**` banner with before / now / unchanged / remedy, and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition marker, a category `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` recognises. `Check Changeset` is green on this head. Consistent.

CI on `a50b8dce`: read from the head's check-runs API, not the PR body. Every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (path-filtered UI, Dogfood shards, docs); the Test Core shards and the Type Check jobs were still `in_progress` at the time of my first reads and this record was posted only after all 48 runs completed with none red — see the status line under VERDICT.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question — numbers and booleans on a string field: A (keep coercing) or B (narrow in a follow-up)?** Answer: **A for this PR**, as the dev recommends and as the card scopes. But the dev's "nothing measured them as harmful" undersells the residual: the arm judges `String(42)` while the payload still carries `42`, so on the InMemory driver a `text` column now holds a JS number — the same judged ≠ stored gap this card closes for objects, at a smaller scale (SQL drivers coerce on their own). That is a measurable defect, not a matter of taste, so it should be **filed as a card (B)** with a seeds / examples / fixtures writer grep as its first step, not left to "only if a card asks". Should-fix, not blocking: the card's acceptance is object / array and every suite stayed green with coercion in place.
2. **Out-of-scope finding — a free-form `select` with no `options` admits a plain object.** Same class as this card, different arm, and the two moved pins now rest on exactly that admission, so whoever closes it must re-home them. Should be filed rather than "noted, not filed" (carrier: none). Should-fix.
3. **Deviation — premise measured with a `validateRecord` probe, not an HTTP POST.** Accepted: the engine insert / update / multi-update door is pinned end to end and nothing on the REST or screen-flow path reinterprets a field value before the validator.
4. **Deviation — `origin/main` not merged (22 commits).** Verified: `git diff fea2dbb7..origin/main -- packages/objectql/src/validation/` is empty; no conflict with the validator.
5. **Author.** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no second author to name.

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the refusal hold against the code it cites?** Yes. `isPlainObjectValue` (#27236) is the right predicate: it refuses `{}` and null-prototype records, and leaves `Date`, `Buffer`, class instances and `null` alone, so nothing a driver or hook legitimately hands the arm as a non-plain object is caught. `Array.isArray` covers the card's `assignee: ["a","b"]`. The order inside the arm is right: the #5922 operator rule runs first (so `{ $in: … }` keeps its sentence and the ADR-0104 admitted-violation sink is never fed for a write about to be refused), then this shape test, then `shapeOnly`, then bounds / domain / format on a value now known to be a string or scalar. The reused catalog key is the one the operator rule and the ADR-0104 arm already use for "this value's SHAPE is wrong for this type", so no fifth near-duplicate sentence.

**Who writes objects or arrays into text-family fields today?** I enumerated every `Field.text` / `Field.textarea` / `Field.code` / `Field.markdown` column in platform-objects, plugins, services, runtime and objectql whose name or description says it holds structured content, and read its writer:
- `sys_audit_log.old_value` / `new_value` / `metadata`, `sys_activity.metadata` — `safeStringify(...)` (audit-writers.ts:2138-2139, 2346; auth-event-audit.ts:386; action-invocation-audit.ts:197); the key-material migration re-serialises via `rewriteSerialized` → `JSON.stringify`.
- `sys_automation_run.steps_json` / `context_json` / `screen_json` — `JSON.stringify` / `serializeStepsBounded` (suspended-run-store.ts:750, 994-996, 1049-1050).
- `sys_http_delivery.payload_json` / `response_body` — `JSON.stringify(input.payload)` and a string body (sql-http-outbox.ts:194, 673).
- `sys_file.metadata` / `sys_upload_session.metadata` — `JSON.stringify(request.metadata)` (field-file-service.ts:213).
- `sys_migration.details` / `deviation_detail`, `sys_migration_journal.detail` — `JSON.stringify` (migration-flag.ts:202, 434; engine.ts:12780, 12882).
- `sys_organization.metadata`, `sys_oauth_application.metadata` and the two oauth resource `metadata` columns — written by better-auth through the ObjectQL adapter; better-auth declares the field `type: "string"` and hands over JSON text, which is exactly why `organization-metadata-decode.ts` exists (decode on READ). The adapter does no stringification of its own and needs none.
- `sys_setting.value` / `sys_platform_setting.value` are `Field.json`, outside the set; `value_enc` receives a ciphertext string.
- Every `error` / `last_error` textarea (jobs, import, email, notification delivery, automation run) receives a `.message ?? String(err)` string.
- UI: `SignatureField` emits a data-URL string, `QRCodeField` and `RichTextField` are string-typed `FieldWidgetComponentProps` widgets; no widget hands an object to a text-family field.
No platform writer passes an object or array to a text-family field expecting stringification, so this is not a regression for shipped writers. Example seeds: the showcase `assignee` is `Field.text`, and the dev's `os validate` / `os build` gate families and the dogfood battery ran green on head (self-reported; the CI Dogfood shards were path-skipped on this diff).

**Is the "ahead of `shapeOnly`" ordering right?** Yes. `shapeOnly` is set only for `def.readonly === true` fields under the `'include'` and `'only'` scopes — payloads the docblock calls FINAL: the insert path after its strip, the dry run, and the update path's second pass after the readonly strip. The update first pass runs `'skip'` precisely because a readonly value there may be a legacy stored value about to be dropped, so a whole-record write-back echoing a legacy object in a readonly text column is never judged. No read path calls the validator. A system writer that stamps an object into a readonly text-family column would now be refused on insert; I found none (see the writer list), and this is the same treatment the number, boolean, date and array arms already give a readonly value.

**Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real?** The latter: `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` is the spec's "stored shape is a string" class (field.zod.ts:153), and nothing in the spec, a skill or a doc teaches writing an object or an array into one; the remedy in the changeset (`JSON.stringify` on the client, or declare the field `json`) is the correct one.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-0whijd`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQjPiXgNoSaEpqeGvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Should-fix (non-blocking, file as cards citing this record):
1. Numbers and booleans on a text-family field: the arm judges their string reading while the payload still carries the scalar, so an InMemory `text` column can hold a JS number. Measure writers in seeds / examples / `packages/apps` / fixtures, then decide A (normalise to the string at the door, as #20309 does for numeric strings) or B (refuse).
2. A free-form `select` with no `options` admits a plain object (`{ a: 1 }`); the two `#5922` pins moved in this PR now rest on that admission and must be re-homed when it closes.

CI status on this head at post time: all 48 check-runs completed, none red (0 pending, 0 failed, head still a50b8dce).
